case_title: Raj Reddy Kallem v. The State of Haryana & Anr.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.406, s.420, s.120B; Negotiable Instruments Act s.138
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and sentenced to 2 years of rigorous imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused entered into a business transaction with the complainant, where the complainant paid an advance amount for the supply of a machine. The accused failed to deliver the machine and issued cheques for the return of the advance money, some of which were dishonoured. The complainant initiated proceedings under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and also filed a complaint under sections 406, 420, and 120B of the IPC. The accused and the complainant reached a settlement in the Lok Adalat, agreeing that if the accused repaid the entire amount, the offences would be compounded or quashed. However, the accused could not meet the payment deadlines, and the settlement was declared frustrated. The accused later paid the full amount and additional interest, but the complainant refused to compound the case. The accused had already been in jail for over a year before being released on bail. The Supreme Court quashed all pending criminal proceedings against the accused, including the appeals, as the complainant's unwillingness to compound the case did not justify continuing the criminal proceedings.
